[Large illuminated initial P]After I had recalled to memory the miracles of the Most High, the mysteries of hidden Nature, and the fiery and burning love of my neighbor: then I remembered the wheat harvest, in in which Reuben, Leah's son, found mandrakes in the field, which Leah gave to Rachel for cohabitation with the Patriarch Jacob. My thoughts, however, were very profound, and led me further to Moses, how indeed he made the molten solar calf from Aaron drinkable, while he reduced it to powder with fire, sprinkled it into water, and offered it to the children of Israel to drink: so much so that I greatly admired the convenient and skillful destruction by that man of God. But when I rightly understood my thoughts, I finally recognized the truth, and my eyes were opened no differently than among the disciples at Emmaus, who recognized their Lord in the breaking of bread: And my heart burned within me, but for further contemplation, I gave myself to rest, and was overcome by sleep: And, behold, King Solomon appeared to me in a dream with all his power, riches, and glory, and brought with him his entire Harem: There were sixty queens, and eighty concubines, but of virgins there was absolutely no number: Yet one was his dove, most beautiful, and most beloved in his heart. According to the Catholic rite, these instituted a splendid and solemn procession, in which the Center was greatly commended and loved, whose name was like poured-out ointment, whose fragrance surpassed all spices, &c. and his fiery spirit was the key to opening the temple, and entering the Holy of Holies, and to grasping the horns of the altar.

After this procession, just mentioned, was completed, Solomon showed me a unique center in the Triangle of the Center, and unlocked my understanding: I then noticed that no woman stood behind me, who

❦ (75) ❧

# THE AQUARIUM OF THE WISE.

*That is:*

### A BRIEF EXPLANATION OF THE ADMIRABLE
### and most excellent Aquarium of the Wise, which is otherwise
### called the Philosopher's Stone.

From the very beginning of the world, in all times, many and
unique philosophers and wise Gentiles, highly enlightened by God and most experienced,
have existed and been found, who
most diligently considered the nature and powers of lower creatures,
and tried to learn them exactly.
From all these, with great desire and labor,
they investigated whether anything could be found in the nature of things that
could protect the earthly body of man from destruction and mortality, and
preserve it in perpetual vigor and an integral state. For by a singular,
divine influence, and the light of nature, they saw and recognized
that a singular secret and wondrous something must exist in this
world, which Almighty GOD had established for the benefit of the human race,
namely, that everything that was imperfect, defective, and corrupt in the entire
world might again be renewed by that singular and arcane thing, and
perfectly restored to an integral state.
However, through their most diligent and exact investigation, they
finally explored and learned this: namely, that nothing
at all could be found in this world that could free the earthly and corruptible
body from death (as it had been established and imposed as punishment upon the Protoplasts, Adam
and Eve, and from their

*   **"sum̃è"**: This is a common abbreviation for "summè" (most highly/greatly).
*   **"reper- ti sunt"**: The hyphen indicates a word split across a line break.
*   **"Protoplastis, Adamo & Evæ"**: Refers to Adam and Eve as the "first-formed" or "first parents."
*   **Formatting**: I have preserved the headings, italics, large initial, and paragraph breaks as they appear in the image. The decorative border and page number are also noted.
*   **Continuity**: The text ends mid-sentence, indicating it continues on the next page, consistent with the "previous page text" provided in the prompt (which was an index and "FINIS" for a different section, not the preceding page of this text). to Adam, the thrice-greatest father, by God himself from the beginning,
and afterwards all the Patriarchs received it from him (Adam) by hereditary
right, and from its powers, they obtained and acquired health of body,
long life, and at the same time immense riches. This divine, indeed admirable, thing, the afore-
said Gentiles, after they had obtained it, regarded as a singular gift of God,
and the highest and most secret art, and nevertheless at the same time
they saw that it, through divine providence, would be and remain revealed to a smaller
part of humanity, and hidden from the greater part of this world:
for this reason, they also concealed it with all their might and utmost zeal at all times.
	Lest, however, after their death, it should again be consigned to oblivion, but
also be further propagated and preserved for posterity: therefore they
inserted it into their books, and in this way communicated many most
excellent instructions and doctrines concerning such writings to their most
faithful disciples, and left them behind: all of this, however,
they so concealed and entangled in allegorical words,
that even now few are found who can draw a sufficient and certain
foundation from it. This, however, was not done by them
rashly, but for certain reasons, so that those who seek this
wisdom might invoke God (in whose hand all things lie)
the more quickly and ardently to obtain it, and,

*Aquarium Sapientum,* 77

& after it has been revealed to them, they alone should attribute glory and honor, and pay due thanks: lest moreover the noblest pearls be cast before swine. For if that were revealed to the impious world, then, because of its excessive greed, it would desire nothing else but this one thing, and finally, all labor and diligence being neglected, a dissolute and brutish life would follow.

Even if indeed the philosophers so often mentioned have disputed much and in various ways about this most excellent art, and also, for the reason just mentioned, have designated it with many peculiar and singular names, parables, wonders, strange and sophistical words: nevertheless, with these changed expressions, they wished to lead and show, with the unanimous consent of all, to one single goal and one single necessary material in the art.

Very many investigators of the art, however, have very often strayed from that secret material and thereby transgressed the limits. For at all times up to the present day, not only common people, but also many other distinguished men most skilled in philosophy have been found who longed for that wisdom: And they sought it not only with the greatest zeal, but also with great labor and expense, and desired to obtain it: yet they were never able to reach it, much less become participants in it. Indeed, as many, fishing with a golden hook, very often plunged themselves into irreparable losses, and finally were forced to desist from its investigation with the greatest ridicule.

Lest anyone, however, should doubt the fundamental certainty of this arcane art, and perhaps consider it a mere figment, according to the custom and habit of this impious world: therefore, with the exception of the messengers of whom mention is made in the Holy Scripture itself, I will bring forth here in order and by name at least the authentic Philosophers, together with their other Successors, who truly knew this art, possessed it, and became participants in it, such as are: Hermes Trismegistus, Pythagoras, Benedictus Iesu, Alexander the Great, Plato, Theophrastus, Avicenna, Galen, Hippocrates, Lucianus, Longanus, Rasis, Archelaus, Rupescissa, the Author.

Since therefore there are still faithful and diligent laborers and disciples of this arcane philosophical art, who willingly strive to proceed to it by a straight and certain path, without many other detours, and are found in many places, yet they are so disturbed and entangled in error, partly by the previously mentioned wicked and sophistical impostors, and by their worthless barkings and pretensions, that many almost do not know whether they should advance further in the same (art) or retreat. Therefore, concerning this art, I have resolved to bring forth and explain a few things, indeed, but true and supported by their own foundation. Even though I truly judge myself unworthy to treat or write about such a great mystery: nevertheless, since by the grace of GOD, THRICE BEST, GREATEST (so that I may speak here without desire for glory), I have progressed so far, where few, indeed not even so many thousands, reach, lest also, moreover, the talent, most mercifully granted to me, unworthy, by the omnipotent feudal Lord, lie hidden buried with me: for that reason, to all chemical philosophers, from a faithful heart (as far as it shall be proper), I will demonstrate an Epitome and Declaration of this whole art, and at the same time also, by what method, namely, they can arrive at it, a straight and infallible, indeed most certain, way, if perchance, by divine grace, the eyes of some may be opened, they may be led from their preconceived false opinion to the right path, and furthermore, the great works of God may be manifested all the more: However, for memory and easier understanding, I will divide this treatise into four parts.

In the First, I will indicate: the beginning and entrance of this art, and how one should prepare oneself for it.
In the Second, through a philosophical description and instruction of the quality, condition, and knowledge of the matter, the entire method and regimen of preparation will be indicated therein.
In the Third, the most abundant utility of the art, its ineffable efficacy and virtue, granted to it, will be discussed.

FIRST PART.

Psalm 25.

*Who is he that fears the Lord? He will instruct him in the best way.*

Firstly, every pious and God-fearing Chemist and Philosopher of this art should consider this above all: that indeed such a secret is to be held and considered not only as the highest and greatest, but also as a holy art (since the highest and celestial good, and the Most Holy of the Almighty, is imprinted and depicted in it). Therefore, if anyone intends to attain that highest and ineffable mystery, let him know that such an art does not consist in human power, but in the most merciful will of God, and that not WILL, or desire, but the MERCY of the Almighty promotes one to it. Therefore, above all, it is necessary that you be pious, lift your heart to Him alone, and ask for that gift from Him alone with true, most ardent, and undoubted prayer. For indeed, it is given and obtained from Him alone.
   If therefore Almighty God (who is the most certain Searcher of all hearts) perceives and discovers in you a righteous, faithful, and less deceitful spirit, that indeed you strive to investigate and learn it for no other end than for His sole praise and glory, then, beyond all doubt, according to His promise, He will also hear you, and He will lead you, through His Holy Spirit, in such a way that you may conveniently arrive at some beginning through means, about which you would certainly never have thought, so much so that He Himself in your heart will sen-

--- Page 94 ---
*Aquarium Sapientum.* 81

you will perceive how indeed the most merciful God will have most mercifully heard your prayer, and for a happy beginning, will have already, as it were, presented and shown a revelation to you.

Afterwards, prostrate on your knees, with a humble and contrite heart, you should render to Him due thanks, praise, glory, and honor for the hearing of your prayers; and at the same time, you should again and again ask that He deign to further propagate through His Holy Spirit this grace, which you have just now perceived in your heart, and to so rule you, so that you may be able to rightly use this profound mystery, after it has been fully and perfectly revealed to you, and to handle it in such a way that it may be directed to the sole glory and honor of His most holy name, and to the benefit and utility of the needy neighbor.

Remember moreover, lest at the loss of your eternal salvation and blessedness, you perhaps reveal that mystery to some unworthy or impious person, much less communicate it, or make him a participant of it; in short, by no means should you abuse it, but, as we just said, you should turn it to the sole glory of God, not indeed to your own praise. You should also remember that, unless you do this, and instead transgress with danger, you will not escape the punishment of God, and thus it would have been far better that you had never known or learned anything about it.

If now, having well considered these things, you have as it were dedicated yourself to God (who does not suffer Himself to be mocked), and by this reason, have set a goal and aim for yourself: then at last begin first to learn how God, Triune, from the beginning ordered universal nature, what it becomes, what it can do, and how it, in all things, works daily in a certain invisible way, and consists solely in the will of God, and has its dwelling there. For without a true knowledge of nature, you will scarcely be able to begin that work without rashness and danger. The quality and property of nature, however, is that it is indeed unique, true, simple, perfect in its essence, and moreover, a hidden spirit is enclosed within it. If therefore you wish to know it, then, just as nature itself is, you must be true, simple, patient, constant, indeed pious, and harmless to your neighbor, and in short, a regenerated and new person.

If you acknowledge yourself to be so constituted, then nature will soon adapt and conform itself to nature, and at the same time, an ineffable utility, both of body and soul, will become conspicuous in you.
For the investigation and contemplation of this art will be so supremely useful and conducive to you that, if you have rightly known its principles, they will lead you, as it were, forcefully to the knowledge of divine miracles, so much so that by that very fact, you will esteem as of no value all that which is temporal and held in highest esteem before the world. Conversely, he who strives to aspire to this art through riches, and tries to convert it to the pride and vanity of this world, let him never persuade himself that he will reach the desired end. Therefore, let the mind, and indeed all your thoughts, alienated from all earthly things, be, as it were, newly created and dedicated to God alone. For it must be carefully noted that these three: namely, body, soul, and spirit, must be in conformity and work together simultaneously. For unless the heart and mind of man are governed in the same way that the whole work is elaborated, you will entirely err from the art.
Therefore, you will be able to conform all your actions according to that. For the artisan here does nothing more than sow, plant, and water, but God alone gives the increase. Therefore, to whom God is opposed, to him also the whole of nature is hostile; but he who is a friend of God, to him also heaven and earth, and indeed all the elements, are compelled to come to his aid. If therefore you have exactly considered that, and have the knowledge of the true first matter at hand (of which we shall speak afterwards), then you will be able to approach the Practice and make a beginning of the work. Where you must again implore the grace and direction of the Almighty in all your purpose, and your work will not only succeed easily, but will also obtain a happy, fortunate, and desired outcome.

[Large initial T]he Philosophers in their writings, both before and after its perfection, could not sufficiently praise this so often mentioned, highest and most noble art, nor worthily enough extol it with the highest and most excellent titles. Therefore, they thus designated it, and in general called it THE PHILOSOPHERS' STONE, or the most ancient, hidden, unknown, natural, and incomprehensible, indeed celestial, blessed, beatified, and triune universal stone of the Wise. The true reason, why namely they named this thing a stone, or equated it to a stone, among others, is especially this: that its material from the beginning, like a mineral from the earth, is truly a stone, and then, because it is hard and dry, which like a stone must be crushed and ground, and, after it has been resolved into three principles (which nature itself has joined), from these same principles it must again be artificially coagulated and digested into a fixed stone, fusible like wax, according to the law of nature.
   How important it is for seekers of the art to know the first,
or rather the second, matter of the aforementioned philosophical

...foreign addition (even if it is called by a thousand names), it must be prepared: whose quality, appearance, and property they have also wonderfully described, and indicated in almost the following manner. Namely, that it is joined from three from the beginning, and yet will become only one. Likewise, begotten and made from one, two, three, four, and five, it is also found everywhere in one and two. They also call it the Catholic Magnesia, or the seed of the world, from which all natural things derive their origin. Likewise, that it is of a wonderful and singular nature and form, having an unsearchable and less known quality, which is neither hot nor dry like fire, nor cold nor humid like Water, nor even cold and dry like Earth, but is a perfect blend of all elements. And also to be of an incorruptible body, which cannot be destroyed by any element, but with all its properties, like heaven and the Fifth Essence, it far surpasses the four elements and four qualities. Likewise, as regards its external bodily appearance, figure, form, and species, it is a stone, and not a Stone, and is more similar to white gum or white water. They also call it the water of the Ocean, the water of life, indeed the purest and most blessed water, yet not to be the water of clouds, or of any common spring, but thick, permanent, and saline, and, according to different considerations, dry, which does not moisten the hands; a phlegmatic water, which arises from the saline richness of the earth. Likewise, the double Mercury and Azoth, which, putrefied and sustained by the vapor as it were sweat of the upper and lower Celestial and Terrestrial Globe, is consumed by no fire. For it is the universal and scintillating Fire of the nature of Light, which has the Celestial Spirit within itself, by which it was animated by God from the beginning, which, penetrating all things, is called by Avicenna the Soul of the World. Just as the soul is found in all members of the human body and moves itself, so also is this spirit found and moves itself in all Elementary creatures, which moreover is the indissoluble bond of body and soul, and therefore the purest and noblest Essence, in which also all mysteries of marvelous efficacy lie hidden.

It is known (which knowledge even philosophers, at all times, have held as the principal part of this work) that then all the requirements, and whatever further its preparation seems to demand, must be performed with the utmost diligence. Before, however, a single manual labor with it is undertaken, it is necessary that every pious artisan diligently recall to memory the given doctrine, and at the same time be faithfully warned, lest he perhaps involve himself with that arcane and inscrutable work, and the spirit which lies hidden beneath it, unless he has first explored it in its deep qualities and properties, and according to the demanding conformity of nature. As one of the Philosophers warns about this matter, and says: "Let no commerce intervene between you and this spirit, unless you have first exact knowledge and understanding of it." For God is wonderful in His works, and His wisdom is immeasurable, and He, as said above, does not suffer Himself to be mocked. Indeed, several examples of this could be brought forth here, showing how many, having involved themselves quite lightly in this work, and the die having been cast, things turned out so badly for them that some were partly killed in the laboratory or gravely injured by some other unfortunate accident. For it is not a work of light moment, as some imagine, and they value it so little from the fact that philosophers compare it to child's play and women's work. Another opinion of the philosophers was that they understood the labor of this work to be in itself quite easy, and of almost no moment, and they indicated it so simply and lightly only to those whom God has deemed worthy and enriched with its knowledge. Therefore beware, beware, I say, and look out for yourself lest you involve yourself too prematurely in danger here, but rather begin all your endeavor with prayers poured out to God, and with divine aid, as we faithfully warned from the beginning, and then you will fear nothing at all, nor perhaps be subject to any danger.

If therefore you have now exercised yourself with utmost diligence in your oratory, and have the known matter at hand, then in the laboratory you may conveniently apply your diligence and zeal, take up the appropriate labor, and thus be able to make a beginning.

	But first, you must dissolve, before all else, the first matter, often spoken of now, or the first Being, which the Philosophers also called the highest Good of Nature: Then it must be purified from its aqueousness and earthiness (for at first, to those observing it, it appears as an earthy, heavy, thick, phlegmatic, and, like some mist, watery body), and its dark, thickly nebulous shadow, by which it is overshadowed, must be removed from you, so that by this method, through further sublimation, its heart and inner soul, which lie hidden within it, may also be separated from it and reduced to a sweet essence.

As an epilogue, and this too must by no means be passed over lightly, that, if any accidental error, or less suitable operation (which can easily happen, and greatly hinders perfection) is committed, a timely remedy must be sought, and the evil must be cured. If therefore you first see that before dissolution and blackness, something sublimes itself and ascends, or as if a red oil (which is a bad sign) floats on the matter.
II. If either before or after whiteness, it begins to redden too quickly.
III. If in the end it does not want to accommodate itself or coagulate.
IV. If the matter becomes so changed and inverted by heat, that even when it is taken out, it does not immediately melt like wax on glowing iron, and tinge and color the iron, nor afterwards remain fixed in the fire.
All these are most certain signs of a sinister Disposition, Regime, or Negligence.

Concerning its subsequent fermentation and multiplication in the third part, more will be said about its utility.

Moreover, concerning the time required for this, namely, when and for how long this operation should be performed for each Act, something more extensively should be said here sometime, which, however, cannot be described in this place with any certain term. For these said Philosophers are of different opinions, since, as can be seen in their writings, one always achieved the effect later than another. But before this, we have warned and said that in all these things, nature (in what manner it represents itself in all things) must be well observed. CONCERNING this supreme, so often now-mentioned art, or the ingenious Philosopher's
Stone, brought to its desired end, and concerning its praise,
virtue and efficacy, and its ineffable usefulness, they could not write sufficiently,
or praise worthily enough. For the Philosophers first
esteemed and celebrated it as the highest and greatest happiness on this earth,
without which no one in this world can attain perfection.
For Morienes says: "He who possesses this stone, possesses everything,
and needs no other help." For in it is all temporal
happiness, bodily health, and all fortune.
      They also further commended that same stone thus, that its spirit
and efficacy, which lies hidden within it, is the spirit of the fifth Essence, which
is beneath the circle of Lunar splendor, indeed that it is the supporter of heaven,
and the mover of the sea. Moreover, that it is, above all other celestial
spirits, a chosen spirit, most subtle, most noble,
most pure spirit, to which all others obey as to a King,
which also bestows all health and prosperity upon humans,
heals all diseases, grants temporal honor and long life to the pious,
but subjects the wicked, who abuse it, to eternal punishment:
And that in all these things it has been found proven, perfect, and infallible.
Therefore, Hermes and Aristotle call it true, without lies,
certain, most certain of all, a secret, the secret of all secrets, divine,
a Virtue hidden from fools. In short, the ultimate
and highest thing that can be seen under heaven, and a wonderful conclusion

   For Noah, the builder of the ark, and Moses, who [built] the tabernacle and golden vessels in it, just as also Solomon [built] the temple in honor of God, and accomplished many other splendid works, and ornaments of every kind, and other immense deeds, is said to have obtained his long life and immense riches by that very thing.
   Moreover, Philosophers also admit that through it they discovered the seven liberal arts, and sought and also obtained their sustenance from it. And God bestowed this upon them for their benefit, lest in their studies and in the pursuit of wisdom, they might perhaps be hindered by reason of poverty, nor, by the rich and impious of this world, for flattery or for the sake of money, to reveal this art and these secrets to them, they themselves, along with their wisdom, on account of their poverty, be scorned and held up to ridicule.
   Moreover, they learned and understood great and hidden mysteries of divine miracles, and immense riches of divine Glory from it. And by that very thing some hearts were stirred and inflamed by GOD, so that they were led further to His knowledge. For through that treasure they did not seek great riches, worldly or temporal pleasure and pride, or desire to obtain them, but much rather conceived all their pleasure and joy from the contemplation of miracles hidden in creatures: which splendid works and creatures of the Almighty they indeed considered and observed far differently than, alas! is accustomed to be done by people of the modern age, who are accustomed to look at them not much differently than cows and calves, and at the same time seek this most noble art for avarice, luxury, pride, temporal honor, and pleasure, in which they are greatly mistaken. Wherefore, first let one part of the medicine so often mentioned be taken,
to which add three parts of the best gold, fused and purified by Antimony,
and reduced into very thin laminae. Let them flow together in a crucible,
as is customary.

even a thousand parts of simple metals, and reduce them to pure gold.

Just as also the Wisest King of the Wisest Kings, Solomon, testifies in the Book of Wisdom, chapter 7, when he says: "I esteemed Wisdom more highly and more dearly than kingdoms and principalities; she was dearer to me than riches; nor did I compare precious stones to her, for all gold in comparison to her is but a little sand, and I esteemed silver as mud in respect of her."
Therefore, those who seek this art to obtain temporal honor, pleasure, and riches, are to be considered and esteemed as more foolish than a fool. When ALMIGHTY GOD, through His divine voice, wished to reveal something difficult and unique to the human race, concerning His wonderful, profound, and heavenly mysteries, then He usually did so parabolically, which parables, known to us in this earthly life, are observed daily by our eyes, and are set before us and depicted. For example, when God in Genesis chapter 3 wished to indicate to Adam in Paradise, after the fall, his punishment, namely mortality and bodily death, He wished to hint and signify it to him in the following way: that, since the earth itself has no life at all, and he (Adam) was taken from and formed from the earth, therefore he ought also to become like the earth again. Likewise in Genesis chapters 15 & 23. When God wished to indicate to Abraham the increase of his seed and family, He commanded him to look at the stars in the sky, the sand in the sea, and the dust of the earth as a type. God also commanded such diverse, very pleasant, and sweet typical prefigurations to be set forth and shown by the Prophets to His Israelite people, if He wished to announce something unique to them. And this Christ Himself, the mouth and foundation of truth, afterwards did in His Testament, and indeed He set forth all things through parables, so that His doctrine might be better understood: as, for example, when He indicates to us the highest blessedness, His divine word and the Gospel, He then uses as a prototype the good and bad seed, or tares—

That which in this matter must be well considered, noted, and observed is: that, namely, GOD has communicated to man, in the highest part of his body, not in vain and by chance, two eyes and as many ears. For by that very fact, He wished to imply that man, namely, must learn and observe a twofold sight and hearing, internal and external, that is: so that by the internal he may judge spiritual things, but to the external he should also give and attribute its own part (1 Cor 2): Which distinction must also be observed with the utmost diligence in the word of the Spirit, and furthermore also of the Letter: for the sake of which, I also, for simpler people, so that they may be more easily informed and arrive at a better and more convenient recognition of the triune stone, in which the essence of the matter lies, wanted to at least hint at it in a few words and, as it were, indicate it here in passing as a warning.

However, just as the matter of the earthly Philosopher's Stone is esteemed as worthless and of no value before the world, indeed almost entirely rejected: so also, and in a similar way, Christ, the eternal Word of the Father, the most noble jewel, and the heavenly and proven triune stone

But in order that such a noble creature might be restored to its pristine splendor and perfection, Almighty God, out of pure mercy, established such a means, by which it must happen in the following manner: namely, just as a more-than-perfect Stone, or Tincture, after its perfection, must still be further fermented, augmented, or multiplied if it wishes to obtain manifold utility and if its efficacy and operation are to be conducive; so also Christ, that heavenly and blessed stone, after His divine-human perfection, must be further fermented and multiplied with us, as His members. That is, we, with Him, through His rose-colored and saving Tincture, must be purified, united, and conformed and prepared to a pure and heavenly body. For He indeed, as Paul testifies (Rom. 8), is the firstborn among many brethren, nay, the firstborn before all creatures (Col. 1), through whom all things in heaven and on earth were created and reconciled with God. For if we, who by nature are impure, mortal, and imperfect, wish to become pure, regenerated, immortal, and perfect again, then indeed that can be done by no other means (Heb. 13) than through that unique heavenly, fundamental, and cornerstone, Jesus Christ, as the only holy, nay, most holy (Dan. 9) recently born, resurrected, and glorified heavenly King, who is God and man in one person, and remains forever.

In which new and spiritual regeneration (1 Pet. 3), which is performed from above in Holy Baptism through water and spirit, we must be washed and purified with the blood of Christ, and thus become one body with Him, and we must put Him on, like a garment (just as Paul says in Col. 3 and Eph. 5).

For just as the Philosopher's Stone, through its tincture, is accustomed afterwards to unite itself with other metals, and, together with them, is reduced into a perfect and indissoluble body: so also Christ, as the head of all of us (1 Cor. 4), unites Himself with us, His members, through His tincture of rose color, and reduces and perfects us into a perfect body and edifice (Rom. 12, 1 Cor. 12, Eph. 5), which, created according to God (John 3), is in true and right Justice and Holiness (Eph. 4).

This regeneration of man, indeed, which is performed in Holy Baptism by the Holy Spirit, is properly nothing else than a certain internal spiritual renewal of fallen man (1 Cor. 12) with God and Christ, in such a way, indeed, that while we previously, through carnal generation from our parents, were enemies of God and children of wrath by nature (Rom. 2, Eph. 2), now, through spiritual regeneration in Holy Baptism, we are friends and children (Heb. 3), indeed heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ.

For therefore Christ died, rose again, and lived again (Rom. 14), so that through this process of His, that is, through His passion, death, resurrection, and ascension, He might enter into the Holy Place, which is not made with hands, and prepare for us a way to the eternal Homeland.

Wherefore also we, as His brothers and sisters (Matt. 12, Eph. 5, and Ps. 22), must follow Him in suffering (Matt. 8), grow and increase in dear humility (Luke 12) and other virtues, indeed, we must become entirely conformed to His body, so that finally also we, who here have followed Him in regeneration and died in Him, may live with Him and enter into His glory.

For since we must fight and contend not with flesh and blood, but, as St. Paul says, with principalities and powers, namely with the rulers of this world, who dominate in the darkness of this world, and with evil spirits under heaven: therefore we can by no means resist them, or their spiritual temptations, by our own strength, but here, following the example of our Leader JESUS CHRIST, spiritual weapons must be taken up, and with these, and the word of God, as the sword of the Spirit (Ephesians 6), these spiritual enemies of ours are to be struck down and overcome in faith. Where it will be necessary for us, according to Paul's command in Ephesians 6, to seize and put on the iron breastplate of God from the armory of the Holy Spirit: so that our loins may be girded with truth, and we may be clothed with the breastplate of righteousness, our feet shod, as if ready for battle, we may wield the Gospel of peace, and the sword of the Spirit, which is, as said before, the word of God: but above all, let us take up the shield of faith, with which we will be able to destroy and extinguish all the fiery darts of the Devil: For faith in JESUS Christ is the strongest shield, which that same Evil Spirit can by no means pierce, nor wound the heart.

Since therefore the regulation of fire also in the Philosophical Work must and ought to be observed with the utmost diligence, and that (in the cooking of the matter) administered without any weariness, just as we have also spoken concerning the Philosophical Fire (by which especially the whole work is to be perfected), what it properly is and is called, namely, an essential, preternatural, and divine fire, which lies hidden in the compound, to which help and incitement must be given with earthly material fire (1 Tim. 1): so also and especially the pure word of God, or, which is the same, the Spirit of God, who is also compared with fire in Jeremiah 23, and is so called, is hidden in us humans, inasmuch as it is indeed implanted in us by nature, through its corruption—

--- Page 140 ---
*Aquarium Sapientum.* 127
...ruption, but again deleted and made dark (*Phil. 3.*).
Indeed, in the same way, by a certain other external fire, that is, by the daily and assiduous exercise of piety, of Christian virtues, in prosperity and adversity, as well as by the diligent consideration of the pure divine word (if otherwise the internal light of grace, granted to us, and the spirit of God, ought to work in us and not be completely extinguished) (*Ecclef. 10.*), help and support must be provided, and by this very means, without any weariness, it must be continuously stirred up and inflamed. For just as it usually happens in earthly matters, that if a craftsman frequently polishes iron, which is cold in itself, with a file, it becomes hot through that continuous movement; likewise, a light and a lamp (*Coloss. 3.*), unless continuously supplied with oil, eventually fail and are completely extinguished: so also, unless a person exercises himself in his internal fire, without weariness and trouble, he gradually diminishes, until at last he is completely deprived of it. Therefore (as we have very often warned now, and as the utmost necessity also seems to demand), the word of God must be diligently heard, well considered, and continuously practiced.

But what we said before about sight, which ought to be done not only with external bodily eyes, but with the internal eyes of the mind (1 *Tim. 1.*), that also in the same way must be understood here concerning hearing. But I speak (so that my meaning may be better understood) of the right and pure word of God, not of human glosses, or the leaven (*Rom. 16.*) of ancient or modern Scribes, which is preferred to the divine word in our day, alas, or at least, like mouse droppings mixed with pepper, they want it to be heard and considered as a sermon of the divine word. By no means. I am not speaking here of such trifles: but I speak of the true and glorified word of God (*Psalm 119*), which passes through the mouth of God (*Deut. 8, Matt. 4*) and is still preached by the Holy Spirit (1 *Cor. 1*): which is not merely an empty and hollow sound, as some ignominiously speak of it, but is spirit and life, and the saving power of God (*John 6*), namely, for all those who believe in it. Concerning this hearing, the royal Prophet David (*Psalm 64*) also speaks thus: 'I will hear what the Lord will speak in me.' From which

If therefore now a regenerated person, in the manner mentioned above, exhibits himself so Christianly and piously in life and indeed in all his actions, then he will by no means lack his fruit. Such a person indeed is placed by God into the furnace of tribulation, and like a Hermetic Compound is pressed for so long by all kinds of distresses, and various calamities and anxieties, until he becomes dead to the old Adam and the flesh (*Ephesians 4*), and as a truly new person, who is created according to God, may rise again in true and right justice and Holiness, just as Saint Paul testifies to the Romans 6, when he says: "We, together with Christ, have been buried through baptism into death. For just as Christ was raised from the dead, so also we may walk in newness of life." If this is done, and man ceases to sin daily so that by this reasoning sin no longer rules over him, then in him, just as in the earthly work, the solution of added gold takes its origin, and, as said above, putrefaction, so that in a spiritual manner he may be entirely dissolved; crushed, destroyed, and putrefied: which solution and putrefaction, however, usually happens more quickly with one than with another, yet it must still happen in this temporal life: That is: Such a person is so well digested, cooked, and softened by the fire of tribulation `(1 Peter 4)`, that he even despairs of all his own strength, and

All these things can be referred not inappropriately to the aforementioned School of the Cross, and to the tribulations and persecutions of Christians (because, namely, before they enter eternal joy and rest, they are compelled to walk through the burdensome and difficult course of the world, or to undergo the school of struggle and the sudatory bath with hostile hoary Saturn, that is, the old Adam, and Satan (John 26)).

sidered and weighed. If, namely, wars are heard, war rumors, various sects, plague and dearness of provisions, all of which are truly the immediate precursors and messengers of our impending redemption. In sum, when the universal resurrection of the dead is to take place, then first men, destined to live through the blood of the Lamb (for the prior new regeneration, made in Holy Baptism, is at least the beginning of this second, true, and now for the first time completely perfect new regeneration in eternal life), are to rise again to a new life, never to pass away, with soul and spirit thus reunited with the body, and brought back into an indissoluble, eternally enduring union: so indeed, that, by the virtue and efficacy of the omnipotent heavenly King Christ (by whom we shall be really, truly, and effectively united to Him through faith, contrary to all human reason), we ought to become glorified with pure, spiritual, and wondrous virtue, strength, and agility, glory and excellence: nay, translucent, excellent, and more than perfectly blessed (*Isaiah 26*). This wondrous coupling, or union, of body, soul, and spirit, likewise the divine glorification and exaltation of the elect, as if in an earthly work, cannot be considered by us in this life without astonishment and trembling, much less seen: just as, for this very reason, even the angels themselves are seized with admiration and long to see all these things: Where then, with Christ, our eternal Prince of heaven, together with all angels and ministering spirits, we shall rule and reign over all things in eternal joy and majestic glory for everlasting ages (*Galatians 6*).

And just as, to conclude at last, in the Chemical-Philosophical work, a brief, yet necessary correction of a neglected and corrupted compound (namely, how it can be conveniently remedied in time, where also the entire process, together with the ordinary means pertaining to it, is to be found) was added right from the beginning: so also here in the Theological work, the spiritual correction and restoration of some miserable sinner is to be considered very diligently, where perhaps one or another defect might present itself in some person, and, God permitting, the horrible [attacks] of Satan, the impious world, and his own flesh

impelled by his own [flesh], he might fall into sins, and either through pride and arrogance (which are innate in all of us, with a pernicious sublimation or premature redness, comparable to the first and second defects in the earthly kingdom) he might stumble, or on account of enormous, great, and carnal sins committed, he might at last despair of God's mercy, or, because of an excessive heat of tribulations, he might rise up against God his creator, and bear the cross impatiently: (which two defects correspond to the third and fourth errors) then such a miserable and contagious man, like a philosophical Compound, needs to be dissolved anew, that is, after acknowledging his transgression, through the dissolving key of holy Absolution, as often as he shall need it, to be again absolved and purified from sins and his daily offenses: then in the Most Holy Lord's Supper with pure heavenly milk (1 Cor. 3) and the true sweat of the heavenly lamb (1 John 5), as if with blood and water, indeed with water and the fountain of life: just as also with a rich feast of pure wine and marrow (Isaiah 25) (Rev. 19) and the public Fountain of grace (Zech. 13), which, like Mercurial water in Chemical work, is the highest poison to the unworthy and impious, he needs to be fed, watered, refreshed, and strengthened, until he also, like an earthly body, reaches final congelation and complete fixation, that is, to the perfect and constant perfection of eternal blessedness. These two most wholesome means of cure and healing for the miserable sinner (namely, holy absolution and the Supper) faithful and omnipotent GOD instituted for the benefit of man, and delivered and entrusted them to His most beloved Church, to be administered and communicated in time of need. EPILOGUE.

Therefore you now have, friendly and benevolent Reader, a brief and simple demonstration and declaration, and also an infallible Type and allegorical comparison of the earthly chemical, and the true heavenly stone, Jesus Christ, through whom you will be able to arrive at certain blessedness and perfection, not only here, in this earthly way, but also in the eternal way. Although indeed both aspects of that could have been treated somewhat more correctly and copiously in the preceding Theological work, nevertheless it must be known to you that I am not a Professor of Scripture, or, in the manner of the modern world, an Aristotelian Theologian, but a citizen and a private person. For that knowledge granted to me by God I did not acquire by studies in any famous Academy, but I learned it in the universal School of nature (Job 12.) and from the great book of miracles (in which all the learned of God exercised themselves many centuries ago). Wherefore also this description of mine I directed not to an ornate and sesquipedalian style, but, as said, to simplicity; just as it is not my duty, namely, to institute a more abundant and copious treatment of theological matters here; but whatever I did, for my part, I wished to prescribe some brief delineation for those who perhaps have not yet made such great progress, so that they might be able to investigate the matter more deeply. Indeed, for everyone who loves truth, it seems fitting that they should by no means pass over the miracles of God with a dry foot, nor perpetually wrap them in silence, but that they should celebrate, amplify, and glorify them. In accordance with that, I also wished to make my confession publicly attested, and what opinion I hold and believe concerning the articles of the Christian religion; since, alas, it has now come to pass that many pious Christians (Psalm 116.), through the untimely judgments of most mendacious slanderers (unless one wishes to sing their song), are proclaimed heretics from behind and are held suspect. May these impious blasphemies and rash judgments of the world by no means offend the true Christian who is assailed by such slanders: Diabo-

--- Page 149 ---
136               *Aquarium of the Sages.*

Indeed, the Devil and his scaly sons have always been accustomed to this, and have shown the same to Christ and all his imitators (Psalm 94, Jer. 11), and still do. However, concerning this, I now make no further mention, but I wish to commend it to the supreme Judge of all, who is the true touchstone of all hearts. (1 Chron. 19. God searches all hearts.)
      Furthermore, concerning the treatment of the earthly stone, so often commemorated by us, in this Epilogue, I wish to refer the lover of the Chemical art to the previous information given by me, deeming it superfluous to repeat it here, and to have that same information faithfully impressed upon him anew. For just as in an excellent song, a good clause is repeated more than just once, so too in this point, the same is accustomed to be done by us: namely, that he should not direct his purpose and thoughts to the earthly Philosopher's Stone, or begin such a work, unless he has rightly known and prepared the celestial (for whose sake the earthly was given by God), or, at least, has begun to prepare both, namely the spiritual and the corporeal (Eccles. 1), together with the utmost zeal, by that very fact. For I, especially in this regard, agree with all true Philosophers concerning how, indeed, without the knowledge of nature, such a profound work is rashly begun and labored upon; indeed, for my part, I diligently note and confess here that without true knowledge of the celestial cornerstone Christ, in whom all nature perfectly consists, it is not only difficult, but also impossible to prepare the Philosopher's Stone. Therefore, this point must also be carefully considered, and one should not, as is accustomed to be done by many, pant so eagerly and inconsiderately for that supreme art (although very often someone will be least apt and suitable for that art, nor even slightly practiced in the often-mentioned knowledge), unless one desires to experience a disgraceful outcome of that matter. For indeed, such a beginning usually obtains such an end, as, alas, the thing itself speaks among many. This, however, is solely to be imputed to immature intention and ignorance.
                                                                                                But

--- Page 150 ---
*Aquarium Sapientum.* 137

But truly, it is even more to be wondered at, that some men are found who not only inquire into that highest art (*Eccles. 7.*), but also try to handle and practice it, and nevertheless doubt (whether it will be a natural, or rightly magical, or truly preternatural and necromantic art, which is acquired at least through spirits and illegitimate and forbidden means). By no means, my good sir, do the Devil and all the impious, without divine permission, have that power to touch even the slightest thing in this art, much less to make it their own and practice it according to their whim. By no means, I say, that alone consists in God's hand and power, who imparts it to whom He wills, and at the same time takes it away again. For to that art, which takes its origin from and out of God, no pleasure-seekers at all, much less dire and infernal Spirits, but on the contrary, such a spirit who is simple, upright, true, constant, and of a pure and pious essence, are admitted. Yet this spirit the secure impious modern world does not recognize, and therefore also ignores its essence and highest mystery in many things. For as soon as it perceives something about it with its ears, but cannot quickly comprehend it, then these worldly companions (*Sapien. 1.*) call it foolishness: and therefore also, because of their blindness, that spirit will be perpetually hidden from them, and finally will be entirely taken away from them.

But lest by this mention I perhaps proceed further than is just from my purpose, but rather touch upon it again, and finally bring it to an end: therefore I wish this to be thoroughly impressed upon pious artisans, by way of friendly exhortation: namely, to the extent that one directs their heart, mind, indeed life, and actions towards God (*Eccles. 18. & 29.*), to that extent, in the progress of their stone and their work, they will daily and even hourly perceive significant utility: which I myself have observed with the utmost diligence and great devotion every day, and thus have experienced firsthand. Therefore, everyone should direct their actions towards that end right from the beginning, and prepare themselves in such a way that afterwards they may achieve a happier end in both works.

Here perhaps someone might object, that indeed some are found—

--- Page 151 ---
138          *Aquarium Sapientum.*

Here perhaps someone might object that indeed some are found who have truly possessed this Philosopher's Stone, or Tincture, by which they have changed base metals into gold and silver, and nevertheless have been little suitable, nor have they simultaneously recognized the heavenly so well: (Eccles. 19.) nay, they have even still walked in the vanity and frivolity of life. (Wisdom 1) To these I reply, that I indeed leave them in their own state, and where, and how, they obtained that Tincture of theirs, I will institute no dispute here. But whether they themselves have made and prepared the true and right Tincture, about which I have spoken in this whole Treatise of mine, truly no one will persuade me, much less shall I be induced to believe: just as also the tragic end of such frivolous men, into which, with their Tincture, they have plunged themselves, often testifies to this, and even today, alas, examples of this are by no means lacking: Not to mention now, that the Chemical art, together with its requirements, will not be unique, but diverse. For just as in other faculties diverse and varied Sectarians are found: (Exod. 30. But Jacob took *rods, or staves &c.*) so also in this art the same happens: For indeed all of them are called Chemists in general, yet they are not informed and directed to a single intention.
     I speak here at least of the true, nature-conforming, and artful Alchemy, which, first among other things, teaches to discern and recognize the evil and impure from the good and pure, by which (Proverbs 2) after the weakness and corruption of nature can be remedied, and right promotion can be exhibited: which then proceeds in the augmentation of metals in a similar way, as if to a fruit, which, hindered by some accidental case, could not reach its proper maturity, you would try to provide help, or from one grain, or seed, you would try to achieve manifold augmentation, which can be worked and perfected with little expense. The other Sophistic pseudo-chemical art I by no means understand, nor do I wish to learn it: (Ecclesiastes 3. *He who to danger &c.*) because its masters promise in vain ways too crooked, and mere golden mountains (which perhaps are too far distant): moreover, this false art grants nothing at all constant, and merely immense
                                                                                                expenses,

--- Page 152 ---
*Aquarium Sapientum.* 139
expenses, reckless labors, and finally, very often consumes the body itself and life. Therefore, if one or more of such Chemists should come across you (who would boast of the true and natural Chymical Art, and try to teach it to you, or even to someone else, for the sake of money: or, would pretend that they could not afford the expenses and what is required:) then be faithfully warned not to trust them too much. For a snake often lurks in the grass with them. (*Micah 2. if I were a spirit of error etc.*)
Moreover, I can truly affirm that the expense to be incurred for the entire Universal work (daily sustenance and the maintenance of the fire excepted) does not in all exceed the price of three florins. For the material, as we also heard above, is partly cheap and is found everywhere, for the pressing necessity, more than enough, and without great trouble: the labor likewise is easy and simple.
In short, this entire art is understood most simply and easily by the pious, and by those chosen by God for this purpose (*Psalm 112*): but by the impious and wicked, it is understood with the greatest difficulty and is almost impossible. (*Proverbs 3*). But so that I may at last conclude my epilogue, therefore, by way of farewell, I also wished to communicate this to you as an addition: namely, that if Almighty God has bestowed His grace upon you (in the revelation of that pious and holy art), you should then use it rightly, keep silence commended to you, and for that reason, apply a firm lock to your mouth, (*Ecclesiastes 23. O that I could have a lock etc.*) and you should observe this, lest perhaps arrogance and pride might precipitate you into danger and harm, both before God and men, and into temporal and eternal destruction: Therefore, you must also look out for yourself cautiously.

*Whoever seeks riches through this sacred art,*
*Let him be pious and simple, and silent and honest.*
*He who does not do this, but rather turns to the contrary,*
*Poor, destitute, naked, he is forced to be wretched.*

All these things, dear Reader, I did not wish to keep hidden from you, both as a warning and as a farewell, relying on the undoubted hope that you in all things (unless God

If, therefore, you cannot understand or learn from this, then I truly fear that you will comprehend the matter with great difficulty, even through another's instruction.

APPENDIX.

If also, because of that gift granted to you by God, you perhaps try to become proud, or to cherish avarice with yourself under the pretext of some economic prudence and parsimony, and thereby gradually turn yourself away from God: then, truly I say, this art will vanish from your hands, so much so that you yourself will not be able to know how it happened to you. This indeed has happened to many, contrary to all hope and expectation.

In Sum of Sums.

And if you follow this doctrine of mine, and if you are pious,
Taking the matter which I reported to you before:
If likewise you prepare such (a thing) in the usual manner,
You will have all the riches of the whole world.

To that intention of yours (if other things become a concern to you), may Almighty God most mercifully bestow upon you His grace and divine blessing. This I wish to pray for you from the innermost depths of my heart.

PRAYER.

       Metals at least HAVE BEING, vegetables LIVE and GROW, but animals HAVE SENSIBILITY, which is more than to grow. I make metals, stones, and pigments from the elements, which I reduce into some mixture and composition: and in the womb of the earth, nor do you need to seek them in other places: Vegetables preserve their seed and their kind in it. In a similar way also animals bestow their seed, from which something similar to themselves may be generated. And, in short, each thing performs its function without deceit: And you, wicked man, who try to perform my office, you depart from me, Nature, more than all other creatures.

before they descend into the earth, they are so tightly enclosed within themselves that they even alternately violently penetrate, and in that way break into the center, in such a diverse manner that they even produce peculiar impressions in diverse generations of ore, and the lower ones follow the higher ones, without error or straying from the path. And then that is another mixture, concerning the first composition. But the whole is derived from the four elements, which, as we said before, were reduced by me into one mass. But that, for your sake, I repeat so many times, lest perhaps you err, nor begin the practice itself too prematurely in a completely preposterous manner.
After putrefaction, generation itself occurs, and that through an internal incombustible heat for heating the coldness of the quicksilver, which indeed endures so much that at last it may be united with its sulfur. All that is contained in one vessel, namely fire, air, and water, which I receive in their earthy vessel, and I leave the same in one alembic: and then I cook, dissolve, and sublimate, without a hammer, tongs, or file, without coals, steam, fire, or a Mary's bath, and the alembics of the Sophists: For I have my celestial fire, which excites the elemental (fire), as the matter desires to have a suitable and proper form. the cold becomes hot, and the dry becomes humid and unctuous. It must be noted by you, however, that the humid will not exist without its dry, nor the dry without its humid: For one is preserved by the other in its primary essence, which in the elemental essence is spirit, and the fifth essence, from which our infant obtains its birth. 	Through my Wisdom I rule the primum mobile: my hands are the eighth Sphere, just as my father established: my hammers are the seven planets, with which I forge such elegant things. The matter from which I make my works, such as stones, metals, trees, herbs, rational and irrational animals, and indeed in general all things that are under heaven, I derive from the four elements alone. Chaos, or Hyle, is the primary matter. That mistress who sustains the King, the Queen, and all the courtly family. The Knight stands ready at all times to perform duties for her, and the virgin from the chambers performs her duty by her command. The more excellent the form, the more excellent I represent myself in it. Know moreover that I have the power to bestow their essence upon all essences, to preserve them constant, and to excite form in matters. Moreover, observe well the three parts into which GOD from the beginning distributed the primary matter. From the first and purest part he created Cherubim, Seraphim, Archangels, and all other Angels. From the other, not so pure part, he created the heavens, or their encompassing: from the third and impure part, however, he created the elements with their properties. And first indeed fire, which excels the rest in virtue, which he placed on high and beneath the moon. Fire has no corruption, and contains within itself a purer part of the fifth essence. Then, from it, subtle air

makes air, and also attributes a part of the fifth essence to it, though not as much as to fire: for after that, the visible element of water followed, which has as much of the fifth essence as it needs: and, after that, finally earth. All these things, indeed, and thus the entire nature, He created in a single moment. He made the earth thick and dark, yet fertile, which contains the least part of the fifth essence within itself. And first, indeed, the simple elements themselves were constituted in their spheres. Thus, air is properly only humid, but fire appropriately assists it. Water is properly hot, but appropriately humid, borrowing this humidity from the air. Earth is properly dry, but appropriately cold, and due to its immense dryness, it is also near fire. Fire, however, is the principal element; it vivifies and causes growth with its heat.

Now furthermore, I judge it worthwhile to inform you that there is no element, namely, that does not act upon another, so much so that one acting will become the other suffering. For example: Fire acts upon air and earth, if it excites the operation of fire. Earth is the mother and sustainer of all things: for all things, indeed, which are beneath the sky and subject to putrefaction, and which send heat into its womb, all these, I say, it sustains from birth. God has granted me so much power, that I can indeed reduce the four elements back into the fifth essence: And this is then called the prima materia, which is generically mixed in any single element. By the benefit of my art, I reduce them, from which generations arise, and these reduced species are comprehended in the reduced mass. Therefore, he who tries to reduce the elements in such a way with the hardest labor and torment, will thus by no means be able to refer me to the prima materia: For I alone can transmute the elements or their species; whoever judges otherwise deceives himself. For you will never attribute its own proper influence to any substance, nor will you be able to proportion the elements or reduce them into any form, as the matter requires it. I alone, I say, am the one who forms creatures, and gives them nature, property,

property, and attributes matter. Through my celestial mysteries, I perform

I will not lie to you. Consider how the most excellent gold received its exceptional appearance from heaven, and its good material from the earth. But truly, even if gold is held by all the world to be the most excellent metal (which indeed it is): nevertheless, it neither cures diseases nor heals the impurity of metals: for it transforms neither into pure gold. In a similar way, it cannot even soften glass so much that it allows itself to be hammered, which the Philosopher's Stone can otherwise do. Gold alone is the best and most perfect of all metals. If therefore, by my example, you cannot make a little lead, or tiny grains, or some fruit from a herb, or much less iron: how, I ask, will you try to make that which is much more excellent, from which both Ducats and other kinds of coins are made? If you inquire that you wish to make at least something chemical, but not truly gold: then I answer that you are much more foolish than before. For have you not understood what I said, that my mysteries are denied to you? For if nature must operate, that is not perfected by creatures.

Therefore, he who now possesses that, possesses all good things and immense riches: Indeed, from a single ounce, he will be able to be continually rich and healthy. It is Elixir, and the water of life, under which all works and things are encompassed. It is quicksilver, sulfur, and gold hidden in my treasure, incombustible oil, white, constant, and fusible Salt, the Philosopher's Stone, which can in no way be found except through natural art and human knowledge, which here provides aid. I now freely declare to you, Laborator, that without me you cannot perfect the work, and that without you, as my minister, I also can accomplish nothing in it: But through me and you, you will gain the work in a short time.

Dismiss the Sophists, or their fallacious works: dismiss their diverse alembics and vessels: also dismiss horse dung, and so many charcoal fires, all of which are of no use at all. Leave metals and other things: transmute much rather the elements into a mutable species, which is the most excellent material of the Philosophers, yet which the ignorant reject. According to its substance it is similar to gold, but according to its essence, dissimilar. Transmute the elements, and you will find what you seek. But my opinion is that you elevate the lowest, and make the highest lowest. Therefore take quicksilver, which is mixed with its operating sulfur: place that in a well-sealed vessel, and a single alembic, buried to a third part, apply it to the fire of the Philosophers, and, lest it become smoky, guard it well. Do this, trust me. Also leave, my son, I beg you, all other species, but take the matter from which minerals take their beginning. I now command you no more, but I adjure you, that you must follow me,

Dearest mother Nature, and, after the angels, the most perfect Creature created by God,

who by endlessly generating perfects such supreme operations through your high

undeservedly at all times, like a mother and teacher, you become worthy
of worship and love. Indeed I confess, that nothing lives without a soul,

your command. For from them you take the first matter, and from the heavens the form:
although that matter from the beginning was mixed in a completely dissimilar way,
until it is qualified and specified by you. And then you assume the
substantial, just as afterwards also the accidental form. You are so wise,
that you perfect all your works through celestial virtue, and supremely operable
forms, in such perfect and just order, that they cannot even be undone by any mortal.

the second comprises vegetables, which have essence and growth:

Now, however, I recall that once a deceptive and sophistical seducer, who was nevertheless held to be a great Philosopher, tried to persuade me, saying: that for the right matter nothing else should be taken than pure and crude quicksilver, yet so that it might be well mixed with gold beforehand: for from two well-joined things something excellent is made, and in that conjunction one makes the other perfect: If, that impostor continued, I were to do this, then I would obtain the Elixir: but first of all the four mixed elements must be separated from each other, each purified, then joined again, the great united with the small, the subtle inserted into the coarse: and in this way the Philosopher's Stone is made. But I am not unaware that such ravings are mere impostures, and that such men are destitute of intellect, and thus not only deceive other men, but also themselves, for whether they are Philosophers or Physicians, they understand nothing in this matter.

In a similar way, I am also well aware that you have said that only the Most High God can create something from the elements, since He produced nature. Therefore, all boastful Alchemist Sophists should now be silent, nor should they hope to gather where they do not sow: who, through their false calcinations, sublimations, distillations, drive away spirits through smoke, and, through their sophistical coagulations and congelations, try to persuade the ignorant; indeed, even among those who have completed the work, they pretend that the element of quicksilver and gold will be rightly separated, which, however, in the outcome and end is nothing. For it is true that all things which are under heaven are made from the four elements, have the right quantity, and thus, according to their species, by nature, are mixed in the right proportion: not, however, so that all are properly united, but distinct in virtue, especially will the matter of the Philosopher's Stone be.

By these things, I also understand how in red quicksilver, and the perfect body, which is called Sol (Gold), the four elements, each united with each other in a peculiar way, and mixed through singular media, will be such that, by the benefit of human art, they cannot be separated: For all ancient and true Philosophers write that fire and air are enclosed in water and earth, in which they exercise their virtue, and in an utterly indissoluble way vehemently contend with each other, so that no one, except God and Nature, can loosen that bond. I can truly affirm this, and also philosophically demonstrate it: For fire is invisible to us, and air incomprehensible: But if anyone says that individual elements can be seen, he is an impostor: since, from irrefutable foundations, the elements are inseparable. Although Sophists also pretend, and wish to affirm for certain, that they separate gold and quicksilver into four elements, nevertheless they are liars.

**A SHORT TREATISE,**

or

**A PHILOSOPHICAL SUMMARY,**

**OF NICOLAS FLAMEL.**

He who strives to obtain knowledge of metals and a certain understanding of how they are transmuted into one another, must first of all know from what matter they originate, and how they are also formed simultaneously in their minerals. Therefore, lest one perhaps err here, the transmutations, as they occur everywhere in the veins of the earth, must be observed and watched. Wherefore they can also be transmuted outside of minerals, if they are first made spiritual, so that indeed they may turn into their sulfur and quicksilver, which nature makes. For all metals are formed from sulfur and quicksilver, these two seeds of all metals: of which one is of the male sex and complexion, the other of the female. Moreover, those two seeds are composed of the elements. And the first indeed, namely the male, which is called sulfur, is nothing other than fire and air: and it is true sulfur, like fire, without a mutable and metallic nature, but not that common kind, which is of no metallic substance. The other female seed, which is called quicksilver, is nothing other than earth and water. These two said seeds the ancient wise men prefigured by two Dragons or serpents, of which one had wings, but the other had none. The Dragon without wings is sulfur, never from fire

--- Page 186 ---
*Philosophical Summary.* 173

never flying from fire. The winged serpent is quicksilver, which is transported by the wind, the female seed, made from water and earth: wherefore also at its certain hour it flies away from fire, and in this it is inconstant. But if these two seeds, separated from each other, are again brought into one, and, through triumphant nature, become united in the book of Mercury, which is the first metal and the mother of metals, then the Philosophers call that the flying Dragon, because the Dragon, kindled by its fire, gradually scatters fire and poisonous vapor into the air during its flight: Mercury also does the same, which, resting in its place in the vessel above the external fire, with the fire correctly applied, ignites the internal natural (principle) which is hidden in the depths: and then one will be able to see how that external fire, which is called vegetable, inflames Mercury's natural (principle): But one a little more vigilant will see some poisonous smoke or vapor exhaling into the air, which will be of such a stench, and a most pernicious poison, which is nothing other than the Dragon's head, which very quickly emerges from Babylon, which is surrounded by two or three miles.

But other Philosophers compared this Mercury to a flying lion, or rather, named it so for this reason, because a lion devours various animals, and by this voracity of its own, according to its pleasure, refreshes and gladdens itself, except for those which can violently resist its fury. Mercury also does the same, which has such an operation in itself, that it immediately strips any metal of its form, consumes it, and devours it. Nevertheless, I signify to you that there are two metals, namely gold and silver, which can resist it: although it will become known that Mercury, when too much inflamed, also devours these two metals and hides them in its belly: However, whether that happens to either of them, it is certain that it is not consumed in Mercury's belly: For in their nature they are perfect, and harder than it, inasmuch as it is an imperfect metal, and nevertheless the substance of perfection is in it. Common gold, which is a perfect metal, silver also, and all imperfect metals, originate from Mercury: Therefore the ancient Philosophers call it the mother of metals; and from this it follows, Y 3 that,

--- Page 187 ---
that, when it itself will be formed into something, it may contain within itself a double metallic substance. And first indeed the substance of the inner moon, then also of the sun, which metal is dissimilar to the other. From these two substances Mercury is formed, which are nurtured in a spiritual manner in its body. As soon therefore as Nature will have formed that Mercury from these two spirits mentioned, then it strives to render them perfect and corporeal. When indeed these two spirits will have grown up, and two seeds will have awakened, then they desire to assume their own bodies, by which very fact the mother, Mercury, must die: Which, thus naturally mortified, then is no longer able to vivify itself, as it was before.

Boastful and arrogant certain Chemists in obscure words affirm-

--- Page 188 ---
*Philosophical Summary.* 175

thus it can multiply itself, so that it may better reach full perfection and virtue, as I myself have experienced, and I will be able to affirm and confirm that for certain. As long as it is also in its Mercury, that is, not separated from its ore, but well preserved, (for indeed every metal which is still in its ore, that is Mercury) then it can multiply itself, provided it can obtain substance from its Mercury. But if the fixed grain is removed, and separated from its Mercury, which is its ore, then it will be similar to some green, unripe fruit on a tree, which, with the flower removed, forms fruit, and from that becomes a fruit. But if someone were to pluck that unripe fruit, then its first formation would be corrupted. For indeed man has no knowledge to bestow substance or maturity, just as inner nature (does), while the fruit still hangs from the tree, and can receive its substance and nourishment from nature. Therefore, as long as maturity is now awaited, so long also does the fruit draw in flavor and liquid, both by augmenting and nourishing, until it reaches perfect maturity.

In a similar way, it is compared with gold. For if a grain is made by nature, and reduced to its Mercury, then it is also sustained by that same (nature) daily and incessantly, and is reduced to its perfect Mercury, as it is in itself. Then it must be awaited, until it obtains some substance from its Mercury, no differently than usually happens with fruits of trees. For just as Mercury is the tree of both perfect and imperfect metals, so also they can have no nourishment from elsewhere than from their sole Mercury. If therefore perhaps you wish to gather fruit from Mercury, which is the shining and luminous Sun & Moon, if it happens that perhaps they are joined not far from each other, yet so that this happens without longer delay: then do not think that you can again join, multiply, and, without change, augment them, as Nature did from the beginning. For if metals are separated from their ore, then they, no differently than smaller ones plucked too early
                                                                                                from trees.

fruits of trees, which never reach their just size and perfection, are found. Similarly, and by nature, and experience itself, it is known concerning the fruits of trees, that if an apple or a pear is once plucked from the tree, great foolishness will then occur if anyone tries to re-insert it into the tree and in this way expect the fruit's maturity. For the more it is handled, as experience similarly testifies, the more and sooner it withers. And in the same way, the matter stands with metals. For if anyone were to take common metallic gold and silver, and try to reduce both these metals into Mercury, he would be utterly foolish. For here no subtle art would be found by which one would not deceive oneself, even if one used various waters, cements, or other infinite things of that kind, which cannot be enumerated individually; he would constantly stray from the goal, and the same thing would happen to him as to those who pluck immature fruits and then wish to reattach them to the stem. Although some true Philosophers have rightly and well said that if the Sun and Moon are duly conjoined through the right Mercury, then all other imperfect metals are rendered perfect: yet in this matter, most men stray from the goal, who have nothing else on earth than these three things, vegetables, animals, or minerals, which are united in one thing: For they do not allow themselves to care that Philosophers do not speak of common gold, silver, and Mercury, all of which are dead, and no longer receive any substance, but remain in their BEING, and none can help another to perfection. Indeed, they are truly fruits that are plucked from trees before their time, and therefore are also considered worthless: For in them, what is sought is by no means found: they possess nothing more than their deficiencies. Therefore, the fruits are to be sought on the tree, which leads directly to them, and whose fruit daily becomes more and more great and is augmented, as long as the tree extends. And indeed, this work, when seen, is the greatest joy. Through this means, this tree, without the collection of fruits, can be planted and transported to other more humid, more fruitful, and better places; which indeed perhaps in one day gives more nour-
                                                                                                    ishment—
