Yet another rare Example, made in the year 1664 at The Hague by a certain silversmith, whose name is GRILL, how he, by means of Spirit of Salt prepared in an uncommon way, ripened LEAD, so that from one pound he obtained three parts of the best Silver, and two ounces of the most fixed gold.
At The Hague, a certain silversmith and a very experienced student of Alchemy, but truly a very poor man according to the nature of Alchemy, some years ago, asked a very good friend of mine, namely the cloth dyer *Johann Caspar Knôttner*, for Spirit of Salt prepared in an uncommon way. To whom Knôttner, giving it and asking, "Whether he would use this received Spirit of Salt for Metals or not," Grillus replied, "For Metals," and afterwards poured this Spirit of Salt over lead, which he placed in a usual glass dish for seasonings or confections. After the lapse of two weeks, there appeared floating on top a most curious, most splendid silver Star, as if prepared by a most ingenious artist with a Circle: Whereupon Grillus, filled with immense joy, signified to us that he now

--- Page 845 ---
832     *The Golden Calf.*

that he had now seen the Star of the Philosophers, about which perhaps he had read in Basilius. I and many other honest men were observing with great admiration this star floating on the Spirit of Salt, while in the bottom remained lead of an ash-grey color and swollen like a sponge; but after seven or nine days, in the month of July, due to the great heat of the air, that humidity of the Spirit of Salt was consumed and vanished, but the star sought the bottom, and placed itself again upon that spongy, earthy lead. This was worthy of admiration, and was seen by not a few spectators. Finally, that Grillus took a part of that ash-grey lead with the adhering star, and cupelled it under a test, and found from one pound of this lead twelve ounces of cupelled Moon (silver), and from these twelve ounces, moreover, two ounces of the best Gold. And I, Helvetius, can still demonstrate a little of this spongy lead with the star still adhering, and besides the leaves of the star, also Silver and Gold made from it. Since that Grillus, both cunning and foolish, was unwilling to indicate to that Knöttner whether he had used his Spirit of Salt, but repeatedly tried to learn from him the art of making it, the aforementioned Knöttner, after a considerable time had passed, forgot what kind of Spirit of Salt [for he was indeed equipped with various kinds of it] he had communicated to him, not knowing how to find the same so quickly; meanwhile he himself was at last seized by the plague with his whole family and died out, while the other (Grillus) submerged in waters, exchanged life for death; but none of the investigators after the death of both was able to discover the art of making it similarly to those two. Certainly it arouses admiration, that the Internal Nature of Lead should appear in such a noble external form from a simple maturation by the Spirit of Salt; nor does it soothe minds with less admiration, that the wondrous Philosophers' Stone can most swiftly transmute Metals, inasmuch as its virtue, potentially inherent, is brought into act, just as in iron by the contact of a magnet. But enough of these things for the sons of the Art.

CHAPTER III.

*Since promises are held to be the more pleasing, the sooner they are fulfilled, I, without any delay, will immediately return to the promised goal of my history to be recounted, concerning which, take note as follows:*

**A**t The Hague, into my house, at some afternoon hour on the 27th of December in the year 1666 from the saving birth of Christ, there arrived a certain man, to me indeed completely unknown, but accompanied by honest gravity as well as serious authority, clothed in a common habit, similar to some Memnonite, endowed with a medium stature, with a face rather long and sprinkled with some pockmarks, with hair indeed very black, but by no means curly, beardless on the chin, and being about his forty-third or forty-fourth year of age, originating, as far as I can gather by conjecture, from North Batavia, commonly called *Nord-Hollandia.*
After the polite greetings were concluded, this new guest, with the greatest reverence, asked me to grant him free access to me, since, on account of the Art of Pyrotechnics, he had not wished nor been able to pass by my dwelling, adding that he had not only long since tried to visit me perhaps even through the obliging service of some friend, but also had thoroughly read some of my treatises, specifically indeed that one which I had published against Mr. DIGBY's Sympathetic Powder and in it had revealed my doubt concerning the True Philosophical Mystery. Therefore, this opportune moment having been seized, he asked me whether I could believe that in the Nature of Things there still existed such a Great Mystery, by the benefit of which a Physician might be able to universally cure all diseases, unless the patient already suffered from a defect of either the lung, or the liver, or some similar noble principal organ.

For experience teaches that as many constitutions or complexions of human bodies exist, so too are these (bodies) subject to as many diversities of diseases, even if the disease is of one kind and the same, as daily conversation proves to us in those who drink Wine, from which indeed very diverse operations manifestly reveal themselves.
       Indeed, PETER, as soon as he drinks Wine, suffers from an extremely angry, not to say, furious madness.
       On the contrary, PAUL, drinking wine, seems to have imbibed in his spirit a timidity almost like a lamb's.
       But MATTHIAS sings, and LUKE weeps.

Hence, foreseeing that something adverse will befall him, he prefers to prevent rather than be prevented. Beginning without beginning; Fount from which all kinds
Of good flow forth, Ruler and Author of Nature,
Comprehending all things, comprehended by none.
Immense Majesty, Goodness, Wisdom, Life,
Order, Grace, End, Mind, Truth, Light, Way, Virtue:
Dwelling nowhere, and dwelling everywhere: Immovable, and giving
Constant motion to all; from whom are all things and into whom
All things, through whom also are all things: always remaining in the same
Condition, changeable by no age:

[Column 2]
Greatest of Causes, who, by a fixed law, revolving
The starry mass, governs the laws of the fates;
King of Kings, to whom a Thousand stand by, and a Thousand minister
Armies of joyful Divinities, singing hymns
In the fields of Immense Light, beyond the outermost
Walls of the World, Where is the most fitting seat for true things:
Thee I worship, Thee I venerate, Thee now I reverently adore
And humbly pray that Thou wouldst deign to look upon me with a benevolent
Countenance, and hear the voice of one praying.
Send me the rays of Thy Light, drive away the darkness
Of a mind oppressed [alas] too much in a dying body,
Grant me to find the right way, lest harmful Error,
And vain credulity and blind Opinion drag me
Headlong into the rough paths of things and the contagions of Life.

[Column 3]
For without Thee, mortal genius, and human virtue,
While it hopes to raise itself from the ground, like Icarus once,
Collapses with its structure disjointed and wings unbound:
Nor can it without Thee discern the innermost secrets of hidden Truth,
Nor by what means or art salvation may be sought.
Therefore grant me, O most worthy King of Kings,
That I may know Thee, and please Thee: then may I know myself
What I am, for what cause produced on Earth, and from where
I came here, and finally whither, having finished life, I shall go:
What I must do while I live: and what I must avoid:
So that when Lachesis has finished my threads, and the last
Day has hidden these exhausted limbs in the tomb,
Death may become for me a welcome rest, and a harbor of salvation.

BY THE WORD OF THE LORD WERE THE HEAVENS ESTABLISHED, AND BY THE SPIRIT OF HIS MOUTH ALL THEIR HOST, Psalm. 33. THE SPIRIT OF THE LORD HAS FILLED THE WHOLE EARTH: ALL THINGS ARE SATISFIED
BY YOUR GOODNESS, O LORD: WHEN YOU TURN AWAY YOUR FACE, THEY ARE TROUBLED: YOU TAKE AWAY THEIR SPIRIT, AND THEY PERISH, AND TO THEIR DUST THEY RETURN: YOU SEND FORTH YOUR SPIRIT
AND THEY ARE CREATED: THUS YOU RENEW THE FACE OF THE EARTH: YOUR GLORY ENDURES FOREVER. Psalm. 104.

THE EMERALD TABLET OF HERMES.
True, without falsehood, certain and most true: That which is below is like that which is above, and that which is above is like that which is below, for performing the miracles of the One Thing. And just as all things
were from One, by the meditation of One: So all things were born from this One Thing by adaptation. Its father is the Sun, its mother the Moon. The Wind carried it in its belly. Its nurse is the Earth. The father
of all perfection of the whole world is here. Its power is complete, if it is turned into earth. You will separate the Earth from the Fire, the subtle from the dense, gently, with great skill. It ascends from the Earth to the Heaven, and again de-
scends to the Earth, and receives the power of things above and things below. Thus you will have the glory of the whole world. Therefore all obscurity will flee from you. This is the strong strength of all strength, because it will conquer every subtle thing,
and will penetrate every solid thing: THUS THE WORLD WAS CREATED. From this will be wonderful adaptations, the manner of which is here. Therefore I am called Hermes Trismegistus, having the three
parts of the philosophy of the whole world. That which I have said concerning the operation of the Sun is completed.
